When I was three, Mrs. Bernstein invited Mommy to join a women’s trip to the Ohel. Mommy brought me along to thank the Rebbe for the miracle of my birth.

At the Ohel, Mommy asked Mrs. Bernstein, “What’s the Rebbe’s kapitel?”

But somehow, Mommy thought she heard 118. She opened the worn-out Tehillim that she had brought from home to kapitel 118— and then, something slipped out.

It was the picture of the doctor’s test, the one that had shown the problem with my brain. Mommy had tucked it in the page of kapitel 118 during those hard days and had forgotten about it.

Holding the picture in one hand and me in the other, Mommy smiled through her tears.

whispered, “Thank You, Hashem … and thank you, Rebbe!”

Standing at the Ohel, memories of those hard days rushed back to Mommy. And here she was, holding her miracle child.

Ten years after her last baby, Mommy was expecting another child—me! Everything seemed fine … until one day, when she was at the doctor’s office.

At first, Mommy was calm because it was just a regular checkup. But the doctor kept staring at the screen, and he looked very serious.

Mommy began to feel uneasy. “Is everything okay?” she asked.

The doctor sighed. “It looks like there’s something wrong in your baby’s brain,” he said, giving Mommy a picture of the scan. “In thirty years, I’ve never seen anything like this.”

Mommy panicked. “What do you mean?” she cried. “Will my baby be alright?”

“It’s hard to know,” the doctor said. “This looks very serious. Come back in six weeks for another test, and then we’ll know more.”

Six weeks! That felt like forever. Mommy left the office in a daze, overwhelmed and afraid.

At home, she called her Chabad rebbetzin, Mrs. Toby Bernstein. Mommy told her everything, and together, they davened for a healthy baby.

Then, remembering how Mrs. Bernstein had once taken her to the Ohel, Mommy wrote a letter to the Rebbe and asked for a bracha.

Day after day, Mommy and Tatty said Tehillim. Mommy felt especially calm when she said kapitel 118, so she said it again and again. Still, the weeks dragged by filled with worry.

Finally, the day of the next test came. After a long hour, the head radiologist walked in. “Why are you here?” he asked, confused. “Your baby’s brain looks perfect.”

Mommy’s eyes filled with tears of joy. Baruch Hashem, the rest of the pregnancy was fine, and I was born on Chof Cheshvan, the birthday of the Rebbe Rashab. ***
